title: Wander: The Cult of Barnacle Bay - Final Wrap Up Review
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Ry8PCL00Sjc

Daniel (@dungeondive) closes out **Wander: The Cult of Barnacle Bay** with a verdict that isn't in doubt — he loves it — and a careful account of why, plus the one flaw he won't let go.

He begins with the beast epic, and it's the most personal stretch of the series: Watership Down, The Book of the Dun Cow, Redwall, and a small taxonomy of how such stories differ. Wander sits at the end where the animals were never anything else. The art direction he calls faultless; a dockside tile reads as briny and gunky without tipping into the grotesque.

His praise is specific. The event deck is deliberately tilted toward rewarding the party, because a game that punishes exploration stops being explored — he contrasts Kingdom Death, where opening anything is usually a mistake. The advanced initiative track adds real positional thought and he wants more crawls to steal it. Boss AI decks make those fights unpredictable. Every token fits one tray, which he rates highly, while noting that Folklore: The Affliction and Madeira go further by printing each token's effect on it.

The complaint is structural: clearing every enemy grants XP, XP triggers more spawns, and the back half of each scenario bogs down exactly where it should accelerate. In boss fights, though, that same escalation is the best thing in the box.

----

Daniel argues an exploration deck must reward you more often than it punishes you, or you stop exploring. Does your favourite crawl get that balance right?
